analysis:
This batch changes only placement test fixtures and the test harness under libs/darkbloom-cluster/Tests/PlacementChecks. It changes no runtime source.

1) Golden/layouts/gemma-4-26b.json line 1 (head) adds "tensor_parallel_v1" to generationModes. It also adds the routedExperts metadata (128 experts, 8 selected) and a tensorParallel block. That block specifies ranks [2], reduction sealed_all_gather_sum_v1, float32 partials and shardRule kernel_aligned_heads_and_channels_v1. artifactSHA256 and configurationSHA256 are unchanged. The goldens therefore assert an existing artifact identity and do not introduce a new one.

2) Golden/pairs/m3ultra-m5ultra/expected.json lines 46-48, 67-69 and 88-90 (head) update planSHA256 and handOffPlanSHA256 for the three gemma-4-26b variants. Mode stays pipeline_v1 and the cut and rank layer ranges are unchanged. This is consistent with the layout schema gaining fields that feed the plan hash.

3) Main.swift head line 66 adds a call to checkGemmaTensorParallel. Its implementation is not in this batch.

No trust boundary is touched: TB-002, TB-003, TB-007, TB-009, TB-011 and TB-012 are unaffected. No attestation, encryption, authorization, billing or provider wire-protocol code is changed.

Questions for integration:
- Whether other batches change the runtime or placement-library code that enables tensor_parallel_v1 for Gemma. Such code would create new cross-rank traffic carrying per-token float32 partial activations, which are derived from A-001 prompt data. TB-007 and T-041 are the relevant entries.
- Whether the "sealed_all_gather_sum_v1" reduction actually encrypts and authenticates inter-rank partials between the cluster Macs.
- Whether the changed plan hashes are consumed by any coordinator or qualification identity (A-017). If so, any change in what those hashes bind should be verified.

These test fixtures alone show no regression.
